chapter: Luck, tricks and the Bourbon Street job
title: Hoodoo, luck charms and bad management
summary: Asked about hoodoo, Valentine rejects it, telling of a visitor seeking luck: bad luck is bad management. Russell tells the George Gaynor pawned-banjo horse story.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Speaking of the good luck business and charms and all that, Ralph was talking to the waitress, you know his friend, the woman, you know, the white woman over at the waitress at the Moulin Rouge, when there weren't very good crowds there, you know a couple months ago when you were there, and she was saying she could get that fixed somewhere too, if she'd go down and see somebody, cost some money. Is there much of that, there's more of that going on, is that the real hoodoo or what would you say that is?
Is there much of that over there on the other side of the river? You know you see over that river there?
Everybody come here, they wants to go river.
Yeah. And ask you but people, you know what I mean, for hand for the gamble and something like that. Yeah. So not long ago they had a fella came from uh, Birmingham, not Birmingham.

Birmingham pretty much. Yeah Birmingham. My cousin lives there you see. My cousin went there and lived there and he got married, we were living down here. So he wanted to come here, he's a, he drives cabs you see. He had some cabs. So he came down and my cousin recommended him to me. So when I came home from work I found the man home, there, him and another fella from over here, brought him over there and the man wife. So he asked, my cousin tell, he wanted to find them people so he could get some luck. You know what I mean? Yeah. So I told him, I said, I said, I'm not going to come tell you to come see me but sing like that. I said, I don't know nothing but that, you know what I mean? I don't bother with nothing like that, you know what I mean? I said, all the luck, you know what I mean? I said, plenty of people said they have bad luck. I said, you know why they have bad luck? I said, you take a man working everyday and making money, he ain't got no bad luck. I said, if something occurring, he just bad management. And Mr. Bill, if you, if you, if you,
Not all the time, sometimes you have bad luck. Sure enough? Sure enough? You have bad luck?
I think so, sometimes. Sure enough? Look, what I mean Mr. Bill?
Well, I mean some people are just lucky when they go to bed on the horses, they can pick the right horse, they don't know anything about them at all.
Well, you know, well Mr. Bill, look, you see luck, that's one thing you can't buy. You can't buy luck. You see when a person lucky, eh?

Oh, here's something funny, it happened to George Gaynor, he wouldn't mind me telling you about it. One time he was broke, but he took his banjo up and pawned it. He was going to get some money and bet on the races and, oh no, here's a different than that, he was going to meet somebody for a job.

He went up on Rampart Street to meet him on the corner, took his banjo along and the guy didn't show up. Yeah. He was going to make some money that night. Sure. No band. While he was standing there, he got just a hunch, he said, I'm going to pawn my banjo and get some money.
Uh huh, yeah. And bet on the race.

On the race. Went in places, one of the horses was Banjo, they were just talking about it. Shut up. Putting the name up. Yeah, so he said whatever he pawned his banjo for, twenty dollars or something, put twenty dollars on banjo. He'd never heard of the horse. I know, sure. And he won right there.
